idiom_name: delegation: a property (or the prototype chain) holding the implementation object
implementation_notes: JavaScript delegates natively: property lookup that misses on the object continues in its prototype, and MDN describes the prototype chain as delegation rather than inheritance, including the ability to replace the delegate at run time - which is the behaviour the C++ idiom had to simulate. In practice the envelope is a plain object or class instance holding the letter in a property and forwarding to it (or an object created with Object.create/prototype replaced by Object.setPrototypeOf when the letter should be reached through the prototype chain). What replaces the classic structure is that delegation is the language's own model; the classic form matters only when a named, documented API surface and a value-like copy are needed, and copying by spread or structuredClone copies the reference to the letter rather than the letter.
pitfalls: There is no contract check at all: nothing fails until a call reaches a letter without the method, producing a TypeError deep inside the forwarding call.
Spread, Object.assign and structuredClone copy the envelope's own properties, so 'copies' share one letter, and structuredClone drops the class identity entirely.
Swapping the prototype of an existing object (Object.setPrototypeOf) deoptimises every property access on it; prefer a property that holds the letter when the implementation must change.
